chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who catches up with the Imam while he is seated performing Tashahhud, and there is no one behind him except for one man on his right. He said: 'He should not precede the Imam, nor should he be behind the man, but the one who enters with him should sit behind the Imam. So when the Imam offers Salam, the man should stand and complete the Salat.'

key_terms.يَتَأَخَّرُ: To lag behind or be behind
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدُ: Performing Tashahhud (sitting and reciting the testimony)

ai.seo_question: How should a latecomer arrange themselves in the row if the Imam is seated in Tashahhud and only one person is behind him?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural etiquette for latecomers joining congregational prayer, emphasizing the preservation of row continuity (saff) by preventing the formation of a 'broken' line where a single worshipper stands alone. It reflects the Shia juristic preference for maintaining the structural integrity of the prayer formation, ensuring the latecomer integrates seamlessly only after the Imam's final salams, thereby avoiding the invalidating state of standing alone behind the row.
